title: Run manifest
description: What a single inference run was asked to do and what it actually did. This is what a report reads to state its coverage, so it has to be produced by the run rather than assembled afterwards from memory.

status.description: A status that can express failure. If the only value your runner ever writes is 'ok', it is not a status. 'deferred' is distinct from both success and failure: the run did not produce a report and that was the correct outcome, because the question it would have answered was unresolved. A scheduler should retry a deferred run, not record the day as done.

completed.description: What was actually processed. The difference between this and 'requested' is the coverage gap, and stating it is what stops a quiet day reading as an unrecorded one.

output_prefix.description: Where the run wrote. One convention, not four.

environment.description: Enough to reproduce the run. Without a resolved dependency set, two machines provisioned a week apart run different library versions for the same sweep.
